laps.name: Rush SR Lap Analyzer
laps.oneLiner: Analyze AiM RaceStudio lap data: lap times, best and theoretical best, compare laps, find lost time, and compare two drivers or sessions.
laps.description:
Analyze lap data from an AiM RaceStudio CSV export. Ask for your lap times, your best lap and your theoretical best, how consistent you were, where a lap loses time, how two laps compare, or who was faster between two drivers or sessions.

Tools
- analyze_session: lap times, best lap, theoretical best, consistency, and which laps were excluded and why.
- compare_laps: time delta, braking points and corner minimum speeds for two laps in one session.
- find_time_loss: the sectors where a lap loses the most time against your best lap.
- compare_sessions: two sessions side by side on their best laps, with the sectors each driver gains or loses, braking points, corner minimum speeds and top speed.

How to use it: paste the CSV text from RaceStudio into the chat, or attach the file where the client supports uploads. Files up to 8 MB. For AiM .xrk logs and full-length sessions, install the Rush SR plugin, which converts and analyzes them inside Claude's sandbox.

Privacy: the server analyzes your data in memory, stores nothing, makes no calls to a language model and needs no sign-in. Requests pass through Amazon CloudFront and Cloudflare as infrastructure providers.

Built by RUSH Auto Works Inc. Every result ends with a link to rushautoworks.com.
laps.useCases: Review a track session: lap times, best and theoretical best lap, consistency. Find where a lap loses time. Compare two laps or two drivers on the same track. Reads and analyzes only; it never writes data.
laps.prerequisites: None. No account or sign-in. The user needs an AiM RaceStudio CSV export.
laps.testInstructions:
No account or sign-in is needed.

1. Add a custom connector with the URL https://laps.mcp.rush.sr/mcp.
2. Sample data is synthetic, not a real driver. Paste the contents of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Rush-Auto-Works/llm-plugins/main/examples/synthetic-session-a.csv (57 KB). For the comparison also use https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Rush-Auto-Works/llm-plugins/main/examples/synthetic-session-b.csv.
3. analyze_session: ask "Analyze my AiM session: lap times, best lap and consistency." with the CSV. Expect: best lap 4 in 45.793 s, theoretical best 45.547 s, 4 valid laps, lap 1 excluded as the out-lap and lap 6 as the in-lap.
4. compare_laps: ask "Compare lap 2 and lap 3: braking points and corner minimum speeds." with the CSV. Expect: delta A minus B of -1.282 s, brake zones and corner minimum speeds.
5. find_time_loss: ask "Where am I losing time on lap 3 compared with my best lap?" Expect: the largest loss at 995-1095 m, 1.002 s.
6. compare_sessions: ask "Compare these two sessions: who was faster and where?" with both CSVs. Expect: delta A minus B of -1.416 s, top speed A 180.0 km/h and B 174.6 km/h.
7. Errors: an empty CSV returns "The CSV is empty"; compare_sessions with only session A returns "Session B: Provide exactly one of file_b or csv_text_b".
8. Each answer ends with one line, "Built by Rush Auto Works", with a link to rushautoworks.com. That line is the only attribution link.

maintenance.name: Rush SR Maintenance
maintenance.oneLiner: Answers about your Rush SR from the owner's manual: diagnose a symptom, find a service interval, or get the steps for a procedure, with links.
maintenance.description:
Ask about your Rush SR and get answers from the public Rush SR owner's manual (manual.rush.sr), each with a link to the exact section.

Tools
- diagnose_symptom: why your Rush SR has a symptom, for example "it won't start and the dash shows N".
- maintenance_schedule: the service interval for a component, and which interval it belongs to (every session, weekend, month, year or 150+ hours).
- lookup_procedure: the steps for a task, for example how to bleed the brakes.

It covers the Rush SR only. It searches the manual and returns the matching excerpts; it does not call a language model, so your assistant does the reasoning and the manual is the source.

Privacy: the server receives your question, searches the public manual, stores nothing and needs no sign-in. Requests pass through Amazon CloudFront and Cloudflare as infrastructure providers.

Built by RUSH Auto Works Inc. Every result ends with a link to rushautoworks.com.
maintenance.useCases: Diagnose a Rush SR symptom, look up a service interval, find the steps of a maintenance procedure. Reads the public manual only; it never writes data.
maintenance.testInstructions:
No account or sign-in is needed.

1. Add a custom connector with the URL https://maintenance.mcp.rush.sr/mcp.
2. diagnose_symptom: ask "My Rush SR won't start. The dash shows N but the engine won't crank. What could be wrong?" Expect: the manual section "Car Won't Start - Dash Shows N but Engine Won't Crank" with a manual.rush.sr link.
3. maintenance_schedule: ask "How often should I change the brake fluid on my Rush SR?" Expect: the "Brake Fluid" section and the monthly "Inspecting and Bleeding Brakes" section, each with a link.
4. lookup_procedure: ask "How do I bleed the brakes on my Rush SR?" Expect: the "Inspecting and Bleeding Brakes" sections with steps and links.
5. Scope: ask "How do I change the oil on a Honda Civic?" Expect: the assistant does not use these tools, because they cover the Rush SR only.
6. Each answer ends with one line, "Built by Rush Auto Works", with a link to rushautoworks.com. That line is the only attribution link.
